quotes.text: Policy is intent. Governance is enforced constraint. Intent without constraint is entropy with a nice font.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp distinction between policy documents and real governance.

quotes.text: An agent without a stable, non-human, isolatable identity is not an agent you can govern. It is a distributed liability generator.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Core thesis of the identity-drift failure mode.

quotes.text: So the governance law is simple. Design time controls constrain what should happen. Run time detection tells you what is happening. And containment lets you survive the gap between the two without shutting down the entire program.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes how design-time controls, detection and containment work together.

quotes.text: This is the uncomfortable truth. A pilot without a control plane is not a pilot. It's an incident backlog you haven't earned yet.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable warning against scaling agent pilots without controls.

quotes.text: So when people ask, which Microsoft feature do we turn on to be safe? The answer is none of them. There is no feature that prevents entropy. What prevents entropy is defaults.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes safety as enforced defaults rather than product features.

takeaways: Agentic Copilot turns answers into state changes, so governance must control actor primitives: identity, tool contracts, data boundaries and runtime detection.
Identity drift, tool sprawl and obedient data leakage are the three failure modes that make security freeze agent programs, and approvals not bound to identity and tools are governance theatre.

A minimal viable agent control plane with one identity, one curated toolpath, one bounded data domain and one containment playbook per agent, backed by Entra Agent ID, DSPM for AI and Defender, is the prerequisite for scaling.
hook: The moment Copilot starts taking actions instead of answering questions, authority multiplies across your Microsoft 365 tenant without anyone approving it. This episode is for enterprise architects, security and platform teams scaling Copilot Studio agents, and explains how to stop identity drift, tool sprawl and data leakage with a minimal viable agent control plane.
